scope: Independent source review of the account-bound notification tap controller, AppNavigator tap hook/handlers, and optional pinned call-service transport options. Other AppNavigator changes and real push delivery are outside this review.
result: No remaining concrete blocker found in the reviewed followup.

finding_and_repair.finding: Failed direct-call decline and failed call reads were being converted to false/null and could then be acknowledged and cleared as successful taps.
finding_and_repair.repair: Notification requests opt into strict transport errors. An unconfirmed direct decline rereads the call and remains retryable if still ringing. The call-open retry loop preserves a final transport error. Authoritative missing or ended calls can be consumed. Existing callers keep their prior optional return contract.

reviewed_invariants: Cold and live responses share one bounded action and acknowledgement.
A captured navigation/account scope fences A to B to A switches and late responses; pinned Authorization is used for call reads, declines and profile/group lookups.
Deadline, disposal and scope invalidation abort requests and clear pending timers; reservations release if an incoming-call navigation never opens.
Notification parsing admits bounded UUID route data and known actions without trusting unvalidated route strings.
Transient call transport failures do not clear the notification or prevent a later attempt.
limits: This is source and deterministic behavior verification, not APNs/FCM or physical-device push/call acceptance.
Hosted notification provider configuration and broader call lifecycle are not established by this receipt.
